glance_takeaway: The page is about picking a vector-search engine for semantic product search (Fernwick), from a four-candidate bake-off at 10M-vector scale. Two candidates (pgnearest, Braid) were eliminated on hard failures; the two survivors trade off directly, and the recommendation is conditional, not a winner: Hearth (self-hosted) if an infra hire starts by 2026-10-01 and a >=4-engineer on-call rotation is committed in writing, otherwise Quiver (managed SaaS) with a mandatory budgeted exit plan - plus a standing override to Quiver if filtered queries exceed ~60% of traffic. Cost ranking inverts with scale: Quiver cheapest today, Hearth cheaper at 100M, with crossovers around ~3M (infra-only) and ~30M (total cost).

F1.note: Matrix caption lists all five verbatim: 'M1 p95 <= 100 ms at 10M incl. 30% filtered traffic . M2 recall@10 >= 0.92 unfiltered . M3 filtered recall >= 0.90 down to 5% selectivity ... M4 EU data residency . M5 <= $2,500/mo at 10M.'

F2.note: Kicker: 'Today: 4.1M vectors, doubling yearly; 30% of queries carry filters' with 10M as 'our 12-month scale'; filter growth ('trending up', 'grows every quarter') and the 100M horizon appear via the chart axis and ~2029/S3 growth framing.

strengths: The glance zone alone carries the decision structure: the IF/THEN verdict banner with the standing override beside it, four pass/eliminated cards with the kill reasons, and both cost-crossover numbers land above the fold.
Perfect fact fidelity - all 15 facts audit as conveyed, estimates for eliminated options are flagged '(est.)', and zero-margin/unfilled-hire caveats are kept visible rather than smoothed over.

The log-log cost chart is honest and precisely plotted (crossover markers at the correct 3M/30M positions, 'today 4.1M' reference line, labor-adjusted dashed line), and the 'two attacks, pre-answered' section directly serves the brief's defend-the-decision goal.
weaknesses: The fourth takeaway (benchmarks alone would pick the wrong option) is the weakest at a glance - Braid's 'fastest yet eliminated' irony sits in the last card's body text and did not surface in a 10-second read.

The page is long and uniformly dense (matrix, five sensitivity items, dual risk panels); a time-poor reader gets no table of contents or visual de-emphasis to signal which lower sections are optional.
Quiver's filtered recall appears as 0.96 at 5% in the matrix but 0.95-at-1% everywhere else - consistent, but a scanning reader may briefly stumble on which number is the comparison figure.
